---
title: "x[NA] returns as many NAs as x has elements"
ref: LEN-08
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '(1:5)[NA]'
reponse: 'NA NA NA NA NA'
attendu: "a single `NA`"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- 1:5
x[NA]
x[NA_integer_]

grades <- c(5, 3, NA, 8)
grades[grades > 4]
```
:::

## Why

A bare `NA` is a logical. A logical index is recycled over the whole length of the vector: `x[NA]` amounts to `x[c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA)]`, and each unknown position yields an `NA`. `NA_integer_`, on the other hand, is a numeric index: a single position, unknown, hence a single `NA`.

The same mechanism is at work in every logical filter. When the condition is `NA` for a row, R does not know whether to keep it and returns an `NA` in its place. The result then contains a ghost value that does not exist in the data.

## The remedy

Go through `which()`, which only keeps the positions where the condition is true.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
grades[which(grades > 4)]
```
:::
